docs.text: Combat Abilities Astral Rebuke Unleash a homing spike that erupts beneath enemies and throws them in the air. Applies Lifted and builds up Astralized . Barrage Sends projectiles hurtling towards a target. Command Take over an enemy's mind and turn them into an ally. Ground Slam Slams enemies from above. The area of effect and amount of Damage can be boosted if executed from higher up. Growth Summon a Mold Ally that shoots spores at enemies. These spores build up Infected over time. Ignite Melee Attacks and Barrage , Shield , and Volatile Anomaly do Fire Damage that applies Burn . Inferno Generates increasingly intense Fire waves applying Burn that builds up. Push Sends enemies flying backwards. Push them off ledges and into hazards for more Damage . Shield Shield absorbs damage. Its durability is equal to the Power meter. Dodge with Shield to Shield Bash . Spike Summon an Astral Spike to attack enemies. It can also be directed to attack and knock down a target. Builds up Astralized . Spore Burst Rapidly fire Mold projectiles at a target, building up Infected . Volatile Anomaly Summon an ally that can be thrown and detonated - does more Damage if the ally has low health.

docs.text: Hedron Drone Enemies Hedron Spike THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON SPIKE - A "Drone"-class Hedron variant - A Hedron-corrupted (coerced? co-opted? copied?) version of an Astral Spike - (Background: Astral Spikes are believed to be native inhabitants of the Astral Plane; see ██████████ for more information) - Native Astral Spikes are notoriously resistant to damage to the point of invulnerability: luckily, the Hedron Spike variant is much squishier - The Hedron Spike attempts to approach targets; once close enough, dashes towards the target - Visual identification is easy: if it looks like a migraine, you found one - (You're lucky you don't get migraines, Ricky) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Spike THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON SPIKE - A "Drone"-class Hedron variant - A Hedron-corrupted (coerced? co-opted? copied?) version of an Astral Spike - (Background: Astral Spikes are believed to be native inhabitants of the Astral Plane; see ██████████ for more information) - Native Astral Spikes are notoriously resistant to damage to the point of invulnerability: luckily, the Hedron Spike variant is much squishier - The Hedron Spike attempts to approach targets; once close enough, dashes towards the target - Visual identification is easy: if it looks like a migraine, you found one - (You're lucky you don't get migraines, Ricky) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Base THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON BASE - A "Drone"-class Hedron variant - Essentially, a duplicate of the Hedron Flux variant, except some of its coordinates have been transposed - Or to put it simply: whereas the Hedron Flux spins along its vertical axis, the Base variant spins along its horizontal axis - Speculative documentation from Research indicates that all Base variants and all Flux variants may simply (and I use the word loosely) be literally the same individual that occupies multiple positions in space simultaneously - (You may be wondering how that could be, given that they get destroyed at different times? Apparently they may also exist in multiple, recursive points in time!) - (So... that's cleared that up nicely) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Base THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON BASE - A "Drone"-class Hedron variant - Essentially, a duplicate of the Hedron Flux variant, except some of its coordinates have been transposed - Or to put it simply: whereas the Hedron Flux spins along its vertical axis, the Base variant spins along its horizontal axis - Speculative documentation from Research indicates that all Base variants and all Flux variants may simply (and I use the word loosely) be literally the same individual that occupies multiple positions in space simultaneously - (You may be wondering how that could be, given that they get destroyed at different times? Apparently they may also exist in multiple, recursive points in time!) - (So... that's cleared that up nicely) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Flux THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON FLUX - A "Drone"-class Hedron variant - Appears as a collection of smaller objects, fused (?) together into a shifting, recursive/geometric shape - Capable of spatial displacement ("teleportation"); actively approaches threats - At medium range, the Hedron Flux shifts its configuration into a vertical ring and advances towards the threat - Upon reaching its target, the Hedron Flux shifts into a semicircle and performs repetitive spinning movements along its vertical axis - According to Research, the identical objects that make up its body may, in fact, just be single instances of the object in question, occupying multiple positions in space simultaneously (...I'm not sure what to do with that information) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Flux THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON FLUX - A "Drone"-class Hedron variant - Appears as a collection of smaller objects, fused (?) together into a shifting, recursive/geometric shape - Capable of spatial displacement ("teleportation"); actively approaches threats - At medium range, the Hedron Flux shifts its configuration into a vertical ring and advances towards the threat - Upon reaching its target, the Hedron Flux shifts into a semicircle and performs repetitive spinning movements along its vertical axis - According to Research, the identical objects that make up its body may, in fact, just be single instances of the object in question, occupying multiple positions in space simultaneously (...I'm not sure what to do with that information) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Heavy Enemies Hedron Axiom THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON AXIOM - A "Heavy"-class Hedron variant - Physically, the Hedron Axiom variant is built out of a person (male, Caucasian, early middle age, apparently hairless, as yet unidentified), presenting iteratively throughout the Axiom's "body" - (No information on whether said person might be aware of what's happening to them; I sincerely hope not) - The Hedron Axiom variant strikes out with four beams of light which converge on a threat - Erratic movement pattern - Pushes immediate threats away with a "ground stomp" attack - Ricky: the way you name these things is weird (I don't hate it though) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Axiom THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON AXIOM - A "Heavy"-class Hedron variant - Physically, the Hedron Axiom variant is built out of a person (male, Caucasian, early middle age, apparently hairless, as yet unidentified), presenting iteratively throughout the Axiom's "body" - (No information on whether said person might be aware of what's happening to them; I sincerely hope not) - The Hedron Axiom variant strikes out with four beams of light which converge on a threat - Erratic movement pattern - Pushes immediate threats away with a "ground stomp" attack - Ricky: the way you name these things is weird (I don't hate it though) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Aggregate THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON AGGREGATE - A "Heavy"-class Hedron variant - Sudden rhythmic movements (possibly a part of larger pattern unclear) - Launches parts of itself as projectiles at targets - Projectiles explode at point of impact - If target gets too close, it performs a "stomp-like" attack to protect itself - Consists of a group of objects (or, again, a single object appearing in multiple points of spacetime?); namely, traffic lights - Why traffic lights? Why anything? (Not trying to be flippant; we really don't understand these things) Lydia M.B. Why anything? (Not trying to be flippant; we really don't understand these things) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Sequence THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON SEQUENCE - Classification: Heavy - Presents as a torus-shaped "swarm" of objects - Maneuverable, defies gravity, attempts to maintain visual contact with threats - ("Visual contact" is somewhat misleading given that they have no eyes and we have no idea how they sense anything - "line of sight" would probably be more accurate, but it's not like we even know that they have sight, so... ignore me) - Fires medium-speed projectiles in groups of three - Projectiles aren't ballistic; rather, they pursue targets - Speculation: given the self-targeting/gravity-defying nature of the projectiles, is it possible they are actually appendage-like parts of the torus despite their (apparent?) physical separation from the Hedron Sequence? - If so, then the Hedron Sequence isn't "firing" anything, it's reaching out to touch targets - (...very creepy) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Vector THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON VECTOR - Classification: Heavy - Visually resembles a brick wall pulled together into a toroid-like shape - Flight-capable in a way bricks really aren't supposed to be; charges rapidly at threats - Releases a wave of "force" (field reports are as of yet inconclusive; tentatively a wave of kinetic energy?) at the end of the charge - After performing the charge, the Hedron Vector becomes immobile (resting? recharging?). - This passive state is short-lived, but does render the Hedron Vector vulnerable - (For anyone unfortunate enough to end up fighting one of these things, I hereby officially endorse a "kick 'em while they're down" policy; you're welcome) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Apex Enemies Hedron Axiom - Apex THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON AXIOM - APEX -"Apex"-class Hedron variant, evidently based on (or a fork of?) both the Aggregate Apex and Axiom variants? - As usual, invulnerable to direct assault - Follows a three-state behavioral pattern as it takes damage: - STATE 1 - Flux and Base variants surround the Apex; damage to them is reflected onto the Apex itself - Fires a beam at one of the Flux/Base variants (chosen at random?), which is then refracted into multiple beams - STATE 2 - The Apex becomes passive temporarily - The Flux/Base variants detach and commence firing bidirectional beams - The smaller variants soon return to the Apex, and a new, more aggressive cycle of attacks begins - STATE 3 - Flux/Base variants again detach and fire independently at threats - However, the Axiom Apex itself now starts launching "energy discs" (best name I've got, sorry) - Once enough Flux/Base variants are destroyed, the Axiom Apex becomes faltered - (By the way, Rick, I know you prefer firsthand observations, and I get it, but some of these things are getting really dangerous. Just don't get stupid about it, okay?) Lydia M.B. Just don't get stupid about it, okay?) Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Aggregate - Apex THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON AGGREGATE - APEX - Hooo boy, where to even start with this one! Intel's spotty: as is often the case, much of this comes from interviews with Dylan Faden (see ██████████) - An "Apex" version of the Hedron Aggregate variant? - Unaffected by gravity, immobile, impervious to direct harm - Because nothing can ever be simple, this thing operates in three states: - STATE 1 - Launches great numbers of projectiles in specific patterns (rows, columns, diamonds) - Surrounded by Flux and Base variants in "satellite formation" - Damage to the Flux and Base variants is reflected on (passed on to?) the Aggregate Apex itself - STATE 2 - Once the variant suffers enough damage, it becomes passive. and the Flux/Base variants detach and pursue threats - They soon return to the Aggregate Apex, and a new, more complex cycle of movement and projectiles begins - STATE 3 - Flux/Base variants again detach and pursue target - Aggregate Apex itself now remains active and continues to send out projectiles - Once enough Flux/Base variants are destroyed, the Apex becomes faltered Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Aggregate - Apex THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON AGGREGATE - APEX - Hooo boy, where to even start with this one! Intel's spotty: as is often the case, much of this comes from interviews with Dylan Faden (see ██████████) - An "Apex" version of the Hedron Aggregate variant? - Unaffected by gravity, immobile, impervious to direct harm - Because nothing can ever be simple, this thing operates in three states: - STATE 1 - Launches great numbers of projectiles in specific patterns (rows, columns, diamonds) - Surrounded by Flux and Base variants in "satellite formation" - Damage to the Flux and Base variants is reflected on (passed on to?) the Aggregate Apex itself - STATE 2 - Once the variant suffers enough damage, it becomes passive. and the Flux/Base variants detach and pursue threats - They soon return to the Aggregate Apex, and a new, more complex cycle of movement and projectiles begins - STATE 3 - Flux/Base variants again detach and pursue target - Aggregate Apex itself now remains active and continues to send out projectiles - Once enough Flux/Base variants are destroyed, the Apex becomes faltered Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Sequence - Apex THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON SEQUENCE - APEX - The Hedron Sequence "Apex" is a Hedron variant consisting of swarms of normal Hedron Sequence variants - As other Hedron Apex variants, it is invulnerable to direct assault, and it follows a three-state behavior pattern - Consists of two distinct groups of Hedron Sequence variants: the "core" group and the "satellite" group - STATE 1 - The satellite group detaches from the core and flies out to attack threats with homing projectiles - The core group suffers damage when the satellite group is attacked - STATE 2 - After enough damage has been inflicted, the core recalls the satellites, and attacks by manifesting (teleporting?) small, exploding objects near the target - The core also manifests Flux variants - Resumes its prior behavior, albeit much more aggressively - STATE 3 - After suffering more damage, again behaves as above, except threats appear at an increased rate - Once enough satellites have been destroyed, the Sequence Apex becomes faltered - (Hey Ricky, this is out of left field, but if we actually survive this, wanna grab a coffee sometime?) Lydia M.B. Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Vector - Apex THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON VECTOR - APEX - Another "Apex"-class variant built out of swarms of Vector variants - Invulnerable to direct assault, three states of behavior - Has two elements: a "core" group and a "satellite" group, both made up of Hedron Vector variants. - STATE 1 - At regular intervals, the satellite group detaches and makes independent attack runs - Any damage suffered by the satellite group is reflected onto the core group - STATE 2 - Once the core is damaged enough, the satellites spread out and periodically initiate a "black hole" sequence, pulling threats in, causing injury via an "impulse wave" - Returns to its previous routine, albeit with more aggression and more "black hole" activations - (Side note: Research is debating if the "black hole" effect is an actual black hole. Disturbing that it's even a question) - STATE 3 - After further core damage, the satellites separate and engage in intense "black hole" activity as before, but now the core also releases Flux variants - At this stage, the Apex can be made to falter by destroying enough of the satellite units Lydia M.B. McPierce Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hedron Vector - Apex THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON VECTOR - APEX - Another "Apex"-class variant built out of swarms of Vector variants - Invulnerable to direct assault, three states of behavior - Has two elements: a "core" group and a "satellite" group, both made up of Hedron Vector variants. - STATE 1 - At regular intervals, the satellite group detaches and makes independent attack runs - Any damage suffered by the satellite group is reflected onto the core group - STATE 2 - Once the core is damaged enough, the satellites spread out and periodically initiate a "black hole" sequence, pulling threats in, causing injury via an "impulse wave" - Returns to its previous routine, albeit with more aggression and more "black hole" activations - (Side note: Research is debating if the "black hole" effect is an actual black hole. Disturbing that it's even a question) - STATE 3 - After further core damage, the satellites separate and engage in intense "black hole" activity as before, but now the core also releases Flux variants - At this stage, the Apex can be made to falter by destroying enough of the satellite units Lydia M.B. docs.text: Hiss Drone Enemies Hiss Guard THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS GUARD - This "Drone" enemy type has been observed attacking from a distance by using projectiles drawn from its surroundings, seemingly telekinetically. - The Hiss Guard looks for higher ground, possibly to gain a clearer view of its opponent. This suggests some tactical thinking although "thinking" might not be the correct word to use regarding the Hiss. - This enemy has better aim with a still target. Does this imply poor vision or poor coordination? Or is this Hiss variant simply impatient, hasty in its actions during combat? - Note that if you get too close to the Hiss Guard, it will use a direct melee defense. Or attack, depending on your viewpoint. - Relatively easy to defeat, especially in smaller numbers. Although, this statement is of course easy to make from the side-lines. Rick Patel Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hiss Charged THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS CHARGED - Yet another known variant from the Hiss invasion that overtook the Oldest House. - The Hiss Charged is a "Drone" enemy that boldly flies towards its target and, upon reaching it, self-detonates. - This self-sacrificing method of attack has of course been used widely in ordinary human warfare as well. There, it carries a more tragic connotation, but in the context of the Hiss, it is merely an efficient means to an end. - Due to its modus operandi, this enemy cannot be stunned. This Hiss variant also explodes upon death, making it a "living", flying landmine of sorts. Not pleasant. - The damage the explosions cause is significant and affects the immediate surroundings, and sadly, we've seen it leave people with severe burns, in the cases where they live. Rick Patel Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hiss Elevated THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS ELEVATED - This Hiss variant is familiar to us from the Oldest House invasion and seems to have remained in its original state even beyond the Lockdown. - The Hiss Elevated is a "Drone" enemy that moves around by levitating, while appearing to keep the target in its line of sight. - When airborne, the Hiss Elevated has been reported to deftly dodge some of our ranged attacks - a skill it has had plenty of time to practice. - I've observed an interesting attack from the Hiss Elevated where it charges the target at considerable speed and hits them with a small impulse wave. Although this sudden attack momentarily drains the enemy, leaving it vulnerable on the ground, it still exhibits this behavior. A lack of strategical thinking or an "all or nothing" mentality? Can the Hiss exhibit either? Rick Patel Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team Hiss Ruiner THREAT ASSESSMENT: HISS RUINER - The Hiss Ruiner is a large, flying "Heavy" enemy with a somewhat ghost-like appearance (at least, to my wild imagination). It has holes in its chest from which it fires beams of energy in groups of three, using different combinations. - I've discerned two other distinct attack styles with this Hiss variant. Both of these are more powerful than the above "simpler" attack, and will thus exhaust the enemy. One is what I call "Cruise" - the enemy flies over its target, firing explosive projectiles from its mouth, of all places. The other is what I call the "Dance" - the enemy fires all six of its energy beams at the same time while rotating around, almost like a rhythmic gymnast doing a pirouette with ribbons. While I might be making it sound elegant, it is a frightening sight. - This Hiss variant appears to have a weak spot on its back. I've seen our people take this enemy down by utilizing said vulnerability during combat, as the Hiss Ruiner exposes it when exhausted. - According to the Rangers' reports, the destruction of these weak spots takes three rounds to complete. Is three the magic number for any other Hiss variants? Something to look out for. The Vending Machine is not so much a Hiss variant or even an "enemy" - as it is a corrupted piece of the decor of the Oldest House, now loose in the city. - Note: the idea of a machine being corrupted doesn't quite fit our understanding of how the Hiss operate, so one could also argue that this outer appearance is just a clever disguise. - The Vending Machine looks like a regular vintage piece of equipment until it is attacked, after which it flees. Is there any joy in this escape? Oddly, some reports suggest the chaotic pursuit is more thrilling than terrifying, almost like playing a game of tag with the Hiss rather than engaging in warfare. - (And, even though the Vending Machine cannot be stunned nor executed as such, it can ultimately be destroyed.) - Does this indicate some form of playfulness from the Hiss? I dare not even think what that might mean for us in the big picture - have we underestimated the Hiss and its functionality for years? Best to think of this specimen as an outlier. docs.text: Mold Drone Enemies Mold Host THREAT ASSESSMENT: MOLD HOST - Classifying this as a "Drone"-type Mold variant - Behavior: gets up close and personal; those big Mold clumps on its arms are used to clobber threats - Regularly builds up and releases toxic spores around itself - Spores are caustic; prolonged exposure causes severe lung damage and death - Typically slow and ponderous in its movements - Smells delicious (which I don't like to admit, but of all the Mold variants, this is the one I most want to take a bite out of, which skeeves me out but I can't deny it) - Do not eat the Mold Host, obviously Lydia M.B. docs.text: Artifacts 1996 Commemorative Coin Health Elements will become more effective and restore a larger amount of Health . Minted for an occasion no one can quite remember. Amulet Increases Critical Chance for all Melee attacks by +5% . I don't know if this blessing can erase all my worries, but I'll take all the help I can get. Badge 11-60 Dylan takes significantly less damage from Environmental Hazards . The front of the badge says Fidelis Ad Mortem. Wonder what it means. Bar Blade Health regenerates slowly while a Summon is nearby. It's basically being held together by that rubber band but still works like a charm. Bout Guard Adds +50% Power recovery but Dylan takes +20% more damage. Wouldn't want to lose your teeth in a fight. Brass Dusters Combat Abilities deal +50% Damage but no Falter at all. You could do some real damage with these. Bug Spray Adds +30% Damage and Falter against Mold enemies. However, Dylan receives twice as much Infected build-up. Ordinary was always full of bugs in summer. The Oldest House sometimes got spiders. Catnip Toy Significantly reduces damage from falling into the void. The smell is strong, maybe it'll get strays to like me. Coffee Cup Health regenerates slowly outside of combat. I don't think I like coffee, but the researchers drank it all the time. Compact Critical Hits deal +50% more Damage . However, they deal 30% less Falter I used to watch my mom put her makeup on all the time, before she stopped going out. Energy Drink Adds +30% Critical Chance for all melee attacks when Dylan is at maximum Health . Dylan takes +20% more damage while this Artifact is equipped Darling let me have one of these to see if it affected my abilities. My hands were shaking for hours. Face Mask Gives Dylan resistance to Infected by increasing the time it takes for him to get the status effect. Wearing one can protect you and others from all types of airborne illness. Feeding Bottle Adds +30% Power recovery. This benefit is applied while affected by Infected or Burn Hopefully the parents had a backup bottle. Fingerboard Adds +25% Damage and Falter while using a Gravity Anomaly . Jesse and I got one of these from a cereal box once. Fork Increases Dylan's Sharp Damage output by 15% . Could be a pretty good weapon in a pinch. Framing Hammer Combat Abilities will deal +30% Falter but no Damage at all. A heavy duty hammer used for construction. Standard issue. Golden Earrings Boosts Falter by +20% . However, Damage is decreased by -30% . The stone in the center shines green and purple in the right light. Heart Monitor Prevents death and instantly regenerates Health to +20% . Breaks upon activation. The tool of someone who saved many lives. I hope their life was saved in turn. Lighter Gives Dylan resistance to Burn by increasing the time it takes to get the status effect. Jesse and I once found a lighter and a pack of cigarettes. We nearly coughed our lungs out. Lit Sparkler A Perfect Dodge will cause Dylan's next Dodge to create an explosive charge dealing Fire Damage to nearby enemies. Is this going to burn a hole in my pocket? Lost Prescription Adds +30% chance to restore a small amount of Health after a Perfect Dodge . It's practically empty, I hope they had a refill. Medical Alert Bands Adds +25% Falter to all attacks when Dylan's Health is less than 25% . I really hope no one is missing these... Molding Bar Grants immunity to Infected and increases Damage and Falter against Mold enemies. Caps Health at 50% . It's hard to resist eating it. Mother's Locket Adds +25% Damage when Health is less than 25% . Even if they're far away, a mother keeps their child close. My mother had one of these. Novelty Magnet Nearby small resource crates are marked on the Radar . These things are always way overpriced. Old Subway Card Significantly Increases Rush duration. I wonder if I can still use this, maybe find some of Jesse's favorite spots in the city. Ornate Buckle Executing enemies recovers a large amount of Power . Damage taken is increased by 30% . It's comically large, can anyone actually use this with a belt? Paper Plane Increases Power for every attack Dylan does while airborne. I guess the articles weren't very interesting. Pickpocket's Tool The next Combat Ability after a Perfect Dodge costs no Power . This benefit doesn't stack. Just enough to scare someone out of their valuables. Practice Knot Adds +15% extra Falter to attacks on Heavy enemies. Knowing how to tie a good knot is the first step to becoming an expert survivalist. Scrunchie Increases Damage done by Primary Melee weapon forms by 10% . Jesse had one just like this. She said it was lucky. Shiny Pebble Slowly restores Health up to 50% while using a Gravity Anomaly . I used to love finding quartz and pretty stones to give to mom. Spray Paint Increases Dylan's Blunt Damage output by 15% . Ordinary had some graffiti, but nothing like the stuff you see in New York. Stellar Bracelet When Shield is destroyed, it restores a small amount of Health but only when it's broken, not when it's cancelled. It fits my wrist perfectly. The Weekend Crossword Increases Damage done by Combo Finishers by +15% . Grandma loved these, said they used to keep her mind sharp. Trusted Spanner Increase Dylan's Raw Damage output by 15% A wrench that's well worn and used. Unfinished Lollipop Increases Damage done by Secondary Melee weapon forms by 10% . Smells like apple and... blueberry? Wad of Cash Makes the Command ability cost 1 fewer Command Charge . Minimum cost is still 1. $182, to be exact. Wallet Combat Abilities consume Health when out of Power . Health cannot drop below 5% from this Artifact. I should probably turn this in once this is over. I hope whoever it belongs to is still out there. Water Pistol Critical Hits deal +50% more Damage to Hiss Shield . Jesse got one of these from a box of cereal when we were kids. She let me have it, so I could never bring myself to use it on her. Whetstone Adds +20% Damage for all Melee attacks and Combat Abilities , but Falter will be reduced by 20% . Dad had one of these, too. He used it a lot to sharpen his hunting knife. World Tour Tickets Combat Abilities deal +100% more Damage . Power is capped at 50% . I'd love to go see them someday, hope they haven't retired. Worn Eraser Gives Dylan significant resistance to all negative status effects by increasing the time it takes for them to build up. If only all mistakes were easy to undo.

It's comically large, can anyone actually use this with a belt? Paper Plane Increases Power for every attack Dylan does while airborne. I guess the articles weren't very interesting. Pickpocket's Tool The next Combat Ability after a Perfect Dodge costs no Power . This benefit doesn't stack. Just enough to scare someone out of their valuables. Practice Knot Adds +15% extra Falter to attacks on Heavy enemies. Knowing how to tie a good knot is the first step to becoming an expert survivalist. Scrunchie Increases Damage done by Primary Melee weapon forms by 10% . Jesse had one just like this. She said it was lucky. Shiny Pebble Slowly restores Health up to 50% while using a Gravity Anomaly . I used to love finding quartz and pretty stones to give to mom. Spray Paint Increases Dylan's Blunt Damage output by 15% . Ordinary had some graffiti, but nothing like the stuff you see in New York. Stellar Bracelet When Shield is destroyed, it restores a small amount of Health but only when it's broken, not when it's cancelled. It fits my wrist perfectly. The Weekend Crossword Increases Damage done by Combo Finishers by +15% . Grandma loved these, said they used to keep her mind sharp. Trusted Spanner Increase Dylan's Raw Damage output by 15% A wrench that's well worn and used. Unfinished Lollipop Increases Damage done by Secondary Melee weapon forms by 10% . Smells like apple and... blueberry? Wad of Cash Makes the Command ability cost 1 fewer Command Charge . Minimum cost is still 1. $182, to be exact. Wallet Combat Abilities consume Health when out of Power . Health cannot drop below 5% from this Artifact. I should probably turn this in once this is over. I hope whoever it belongs to is still out there. Water Pistol Critical Hits deal +50% more Damage to Hiss Shield . Jesse got one of these from a box of cereal when we were kids. She let me have it, so I could never bring myself to use it on her. Whetstone Adds +20% Damage for all Melee attacks and Combat Abilities , but Falter will be reduced by 20% . Dad had one of these, too. He used it a lot to sharpen his hunting knife. World Tour Tickets Combat Abilities deal +100% more Damage . Power is capped at 50% . I'd love to go see them someday, hope they haven't retired. Worn Eraser Gives Dylan significant resistance to all negative status effects by increasing the time it takes for them to build up. If only all mistakes were easy to undo.
